— According to the German newspaper BILD, Russia has presented an unofficial proposal outlining a “new European security order” as part of a potential settlement to end the war in Ukraine.
The reported terms include:
• Donbas: Russia would gain full control of Donetsk and Luhansk, including territories still under Ukrainian control, while retaining its other occupied Ukrainian territories.
• Southern Ukraine: The ports of Odesa and Mykolaiv would be demilitarized and prohibited from serving as naval bases.
• Maritime access: New freedom-of-navigation arrangements would be established in the Black Sea and Baltic Sea.
• Baltic states: No NATO military bases would be permitted in Estonia, Latvia, or Lithuania, despite their continued membership in the alliance.
• Finland: Helsinki would withdraw from NATO and return to its pre-2023 status.
• Ukraine: Kyiv would remain permanently non-aligned and abandon its NATO membership ambitions, although EU accession would not be ruled out.
• Moldova: The country would be federalized, incorporating Gagauzia and Transnistria, with both regions granted the right to hold secession referendums if Moldova pursues EU membership or closer ties with Romania. Russia, in turn, would withdraw its troops from Transnistria.
In exchange, Russia would withdraw its nuclear weapons from Belarus and refrain from deploying intermediate-range missiles there.
Kremlin spokesman Dmitry Peskov denied that Moscow had demanded Finland's withdrawal from NATO, stating that the issue had not been discussed.
Finnish officials, including Defence Minister Antti Häkkänen, rejected the reported proposal as "absolutely outrageous" and non-negotiable.
